lots.title: Provision of Water Risk Assessments (Legionella Survey)
lots.description: Service Specification for Water Management Surveys (Legionella Surveys and Water Risk Assessments) for the London Borough of Bexley's operational estate. Contract commences April 2026 for a period of 3 + 2 years. The Supplier provides all expertise, staff, labour, materials and equipment to conduct Water Risk Assessments (WRAs) across Council Sites, deliver site-specific Water Hygiene Management Plans, maintain a RAG-rated remedial programme, provide Legionella training, and integrate monitoring/reporting with the Council's CAFM system (TF Cloud) and Asset Management System (TF Cloud / Civica). Substantive scope is driven by Appendix 1 - Bexley Water Risk Assessment - Price Matrix and the Building List (Appendix A).
requirements: Provide a service that enables and supports the Council's activities through delivery of fully-functioning, comfortable, high quality, safe environments.
Provide all expertise, staff, labour, materials, equipment and resources for the undertaking of Legionella Surveys.
Work alongside and in collaboration with the Council client team and other suppliers (including third-party suppliers); provide a named representative who will oversee provision of the Service.
Conduct Water Risk Assessments as instructed; certain establishments may have specific requirements amendable at the Council's discretion.

In collaboration with the Council, prepare an annual schedule of Water Risk Assessments aligned with Appendix 1 - Bexley Water Risk Assessment - Price Matrix, indicating whether each activity is a statutory compliance requirement or a best practice service; submit for Council approval.
Cooperate fully with Council-directed adjustments to site visit timing and related activities at no additional cost.

On discovering or suspecting asbestos, immediately cease work and notify the Council; do not disturb or remove ACM without Council agreement and full compliance with the Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012; consult and sign the site-specific Asbestos Risk Management Plan before commencing work.

Agree access and security arrangements for each Site during mobilisation (including alarm training); a designated person must retain issued Keys and maintain secure access records; provide written 24-hour access contact details to the FM Team.

Maintain the Council's key handover and return system throughout the Contract Period; immediately report any lost or damaged Keys (costs of replacement, lock changes, door/gate replacement or security reprogramming are recoverable from the Contractor).
Ensure all Employees comply with the Council's 'No Smoking' policy across all Sites including external areas.
Do not move any equipment, furniture or specialist items identified by the Council unless expressly authorised for specialist maintenance (including systems in use or of high value).
Comply with the Approved Code of Practice (ACOP) L8, HSE Guidance HSG 274 Parts 1-3, and BSI 8580:2010 for all Water Hygiene service delivery.

Inspect hygiene conditions of hot and cold water systems at all contracted sites, including mains distribution, stored water tanks, calorifiers, and associated outlets such as wash hand basins and showers, as outlined in the Building List (Appendix A).

Produce a Water Hygiene Assessment report for each site within ten days of inspection, containing risk summaries, executive summary, site details, schematic drawings of all water systems, photographic evidence, detailed risk estimation methodology and technical data.

Report any immediate risks identified during inspection to the FM Team while the inspector is still on site; communicate any high-priority remedial work to the FM Team via email within 48 hours of inspection, in advance of the full report.
Provide all monitoring and reporting documentation electronically via the Council's CAFM system (TF Cloud) or by email until CAFM integration is complete.
Categorise risks using high / medium / low rating; use schematic line diagrams and photographs to highlight risks; include clear observations, remedies and recommendations in each site report.
Submit sample documentation demonstrating the reporting requirements with the bid.

Prioritise remedial works identified in individual site assessments and compile them into an overall prioritised work programme (RAG report) in Microsoft Excel format, updated monthly and shared with the FM Team.

Identify and report any areas of perceived or actual risk that could compromise Bexley's compliance with regulations and ACOPs; review adequacy of existing risk assessments and advise on updates or revisions.

Develop and maintain a site-specific Water Hygiene Management Plan for each location incorporating WRA findings, detailing control measures, monitoring regimes and responsibilities for managing Legionella risks.

Establish a proactive monitoring programme including temperature checks, inspection of tanks and calorifiers, flushing regimes, and biocide dosing where applicable; record electronically via TF Cloud (CAFM) or email until integration completes.
Review WRAs annually or sooner if there are significant changes to water systems, occupancy or usage; advise the Council when reassessment is required.
Complete a Dynamic Risk Assessment prior to any planned or reactive works and upload to the CAFM system; completion of the dynamic risk assessment is mandatory.

Support internal and external audits by maintaining accurate records and demonstrating compliance with HSE guidance; provide monthly performance reports covering water hygiene KPIs, risk status updates and remedial progress.
Ensure all operatives involved in water hygiene management are trained in Legionella control procedures and hold relevant certifications; submit training records annually.

Use the Council's Asset Management System (TF Cloud / Civica) to complete work and manage invoicing; update the system on job completion with date, time and supporting documentation; submit payment applications only through the Asset Management System (invoices in any other format will not be accepted).
Quote the system-generated reference number for each statutory compliance instruction in all communications with the Council.

Carry out all statutory inspections in accordance with the relevant standards specified by the Council; the schedule of buildings where inspections may be instructed is detailed in Appendix 1 - Bexley Water Risk Assessment - Price Matrix.
Comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974, all relevant statutory provisions under that Act, applicable safety legislation, codes of practice and HSE Good Practice Guidance Notes.
Submit a Risk Assessment and Method Statement (RAMS) for Council approval prior to commencing any works on site, covering all services detailed in the specification.
Assume presence of asbestos-containing materials in plant rooms and appliances unless proven otherwise.

Update Workplace Risk Assessments for own work areas and those of the Council; keep accessible to the Council; collaborate with Council staff to ensure compliance with personal and data protection regulations.
Designate a single point of contact for all professional health and safety advice; understand which incidents are reportable under RIDDOR and report all near misses to the Council.
Perform 'Authorised Person' duties required under Health and Safety regulations for monitoring and professional oversight.

Adhere to the Environmental Policy (Appendix C) where possible, supporting the Council's Social Value and carbon reduction objectives; submit details of Company Environmental Policy with practical illustrations.

Provide Water Management awareness training courses for Council staff and suppliers; advise on future changes in Regulation and duties under ACOP L8; provide specialist advice on all matters relating to ACOP L8.
Provide a detailed organisational structure including escalation routes, roles and responsibilities during mobilisation.

Ensure all staff assigned to the Contract have appropriate skills, knowledge and experience; cover absences to maintain service continuity; senior staff must possess excellent verbal and written English communication skills.
Ensure all staff (and subcontractors) have undergone appropriate Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) checks, with records available for Council inspection.

Replace any Contractor personnel whose removal is requested by the Council (for failure to meet Code of Conduct standards in Appendix D) within five (5) working days with suitably qualified personnel.

Comply with Council staffing policies while working on Council Sites; sign and adhere to a confidentiality policy agreed with the Council; follow site sign-in/sign-out procedures and carry company-issued identification.

Engage sub-contractors only subject to technical evaluation and Council prior approval; retain full responsibility for performance and compliance of all subcontracted services; ensure sub-contractor DBS checks; monitor via KPIs, spot-checks and regular management meetings.

Refer all complaints immediately to the FM Client Unit; rectify service failures within SLA timeframes; maintain a complaints log and notify the Contract Administrator within 24 hours with full details and corrective actions.

Treat all users (Council Members, Representatives and stakeholders) promptly, courteously and effectively; submit a schedule of complaints and actions to the Authorised Officer at monthly operational contract meetings; implement a formal complaints procedure included in the tender submission.

During mobilisation: configure IT and reporting systems; agree report format and content; establish meeting and reporting schedule; finalise the Water Risk Assessment programme of work; confirm KPIs; present all initialisation documents at the mobilisation meeting.
Proactively propose new technologies, materials and methods that support greater efficiency, improved service outcomes and better value for money.

warnings.message: No CPV codes are stated inside this specification document. Notice-level CPV context (50700000-2, 50750000-7, 71315000-9) was deliberately not copied into the lot's cpv_codes array because no evidence anchor exists inside the document itself; daemon should rely on the parent notice row for CPV at the notice level.

The document does not include a formal evaluation/scoring table (weightings, MEAT criteria). The 'evaluation_criteria' emitted here are bid-submission requirements that the document explicitly requires to be supplied with the tender (sample documentation, environmental policy, complaints procedure, continuous-improvement initiatives). Formal weighted evaluation criteria are expected in the ITT / Schedule 3, which is referenced elsewhere but not embedded here.

The specification references Appendix 1 (Bexley Water Risk Assessment - Price Matrix), Appendix A (Building List), Appendix B (indicative process map), Appendix C (Environmental Policy) and Appendix D (Code of Conduct). None of these appendices are embedded in this document; substantive asset coverage, pricing scope and workflow detail therefore live outside this extraction.

Contents list omits item 10 (jumps from 9 to 11 Complaints), but section body includes '## 10 Sub Contractors' between '## 9' and '## 11 Complaints'. This was treated as a ToC typo, not a missing section.

document_extractions.page_count = 0 and table_count = 0 for this extraction, so physical page numbers are not reliable. Page refs in evidence_anchors are derived from the document's contents index (e.g. 'p.5' from 'Specification of Services ... 5') rather than Docling page metadata.
Section 3 repeats the ACOP L8 / HSG 274 / BSI 8580:2010 compliance paragraph twice verbatim. Requirements were deduplicated in the output.
